Elena — thanks for the clear list and the redlines. Appreciated. High-level response and proposed next steps below.

Short answer to each ask:
- No-training commitment: We can offer an explicit operational "no-training" commitment for customer-provided prompts and model responses by default (we will add language to the DPA/DPA Exhibit). This will be operationally enforced — data used for service operation only, not for model improvement.
- Ownership: Output ownership can be affirmed in the agreement (customer retains rights to prompts/responses).
- Evidence package: We will provide an evidence packet that includes: current subprocessor roster, SOC 2 Type II report summary, dataflow diagram, and an operations note describing request handling (KV caching rules, ephemerality, and retention).
- Exportability & POD: We support API export and SFTP transfer. We can run a one-time sample export into your SFTP and include export logs and a verification checksum. Proof-of-deletion will be documented in the ops note and we can provide export logs showing TTL-based deletion of ephemeral KV caches.
- Cross-border: We can isolate EU workload to EU-hosted clusters or provide SCCs/adequate safeguards where needed.

We do have a short exhibited "No-Train Operations Checklist" that explains the technical controls and audit artifacts. I propose the following near-term MAP: 
1) By Mon 11/30 — Redwood sends evidence packet and a draft DPA exhibit with the no-training clause.
2) By Wed 12/2 — VetroHealth reviews and returns any narrow redlines.
3) By Fri 12/4 — We run a test export to your SFTP and provide logs.
4) By Mon 12/7 — Finalize DPA and sign (target).

For the ops/technical folks: Grace — can you attach the checklist and a short CSV of the current subprocessor roster and indicate KMS availability for customer-managed keys? Laura — please review suggested DPA language below and call out any deviations that need exec sign-off (we may need an SLA carveout if very large offloads are needed).

Let me know if that timeline works. Happy to do a 30-min sync with your security/privacy team early next week.

Best,

Elena / Karthik — looping in a couple legal ops notes so we have a clear, contract-ready position.

Draft positions and clarifications (legal):
1) "No-training" vs "No-derive": We typically propose a clause that prohibits using customer-provided content to further train or update model weights or prompt tuning, and also prohibits derivative-model creation based on identifiable customer data ("no-train / no-derive"). This is stronger than a plain "no-training" statement and reduces ambiguity.
2) Ownership: We will include an affirmative IP clause that customer retains ownership of input/output content. Redwood will retain service telemetry only for troubleshooting, aggregated metrics, and platform health (non-identifying). We will provide a redline that adds a narrow definition of "Service Data" and a carveout for aggregated telemetry.
3) Evidence: We can produce an "evidence bundle" as an onboarding artifact: subprocessor CSV, SOC 2 summary, excerpted logs (export & deletion), and a signed operations affidavit (one-page) from our privacy team confirming controls. The affidavit can be included as Exhibit B.
4) Retention & Proof-of-deletion: Recommend a TTL-based retention with a documented process for manual deletion requests. For higher-assurance customers, we can offer periodic attestations and sample deletion logs (redact any unrelated customer IDs).
5) SLA/Capacity carveout: If VetroHealth requests frequent large exports (e.g., daily full dataset dumps), we will propose Redwood Dedicated or reserved capacity for predictable throughput and a separate fee; otherwise the standard service supports scheduled on-demand exports with best-effort throughput.

Next steps from our side: I will draft the DPA exhibit language (clearly labeled "No-Train / No-Derive Exhibit"), attach the evidence bundle, and coordinate with ops for the sample export. We should be able to turn those materials around by EOD Mon 11/30.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
